title: Friend bombed an exam
situation: A friend texts you, upset that they did terribly on a test.
tip: When a friend vents, lead with empathy (헐, 어떡해, 고생했어) before asking what happened — comforting first, then a follow-up question, is the natural flow.

turns.en: I totally bombed the exam ㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: React with sympathy and ask how bad it was.

choices.en: Oh no. Was it really hard?
choices.feedback: 헐 어떡해 reacts with concern, then 많이 어려웠어? gently asks what happened.

choices.en: Your exam results were poor (formal).
choices.feedback: Way too formal and stiff — friends never talk like this.

choices.en: I bombed my exam too.
choices.feedback: Makes it about you instead of comforting them first.

turns.ko: 응 한 문제도 제대로 못 풀었어 진짜ㅠ
turns.en: Yeah I couldn't even solve a single question properly ㅠ

turns.prompt: Show you feel for them and tell them not to stress too much.

choices.en: Aw… don't stress about it too much
choices.feedback: 아이고 + 스트레스받지 마 is warm, casual comfort.

choices.en: You should have studied harder (formal/scolding).
choices.feedback: Scolding and formal — the opposite of comforting a friend.

choices.en: So what'd you get?
choices.feedback: Prying for the number right now feels cold when they're already down.

turns.ko: 위로해 줘서 고마워ㅠㅠ 술이나 마시러 갈까
turns.en: Thanks for comforting me ㅠㅠ Wanna go grab a drink or something?

turns.prompt: Agree and offer to treat them.

choices.en: Deal! I'll treat you today
choices.feedback: 콜 + 내가 쏠게 is super natural — agreeing and offering to pay.

choices.en: I do not drink (formal).
choices.feedback: Too formal, and it shuts the plan down.

choices.en: Do well on the next exam (polite).
choices.feedback: -세요 is polite, but it mismatches the close-friend register and ignores the invitation.

turns.en: Oh really? You're the best, seriously

turns.prompt: Brush it off and say let's go.

choices.en: Of course lol see you later!
choices.feedback: 당연하지 + 이따 보자 is the perfect casual wrap-up.

choices.en: Don't mention it (polite).
choices.feedback: 별말씀을요 is polite/formal — friends say 당연하지 or 뭘ㅋㅋ.

choices.en: Then I'll take my leave (very formal).
choices.feedback: Extremely formal sign-off — completely wrong for a friend.

title: Buried in assignments
situation: A friend texts that they're drowning in assignments all due at once.
tip: Commiserating (나도, 그니까, 헐) signals you're on their side; pair it with a question like 언제까지야? to keep the venting going.

turns.en: I've got a mountain of assignments, I'm seriously dying

turns.prompt: React and ask when they're due.

choices.en: Whoa, how many? When are they due?
choices.feedback: 헐 + two quick follow-ups keeps them venting and shows you care.

choices.en: You must be struggling with so much work (polite).
choices.feedback: 요 makes it formal — friends drop the 요.

choices.en: It's better to do assignments ahead of time.
choices.feedback: Sounds preachy — not what they want to hear mid-panic.

turns.ko: 세 개… 셋 다 내일까지야ㅋㅋㅋ 망했어
turns.en: Three… all three are due tomorrow lol I'm doomed.

choices.en: What, how are you gonna finish all that ㅠㅠ
choices.feedback: Genuine 'how is that even possible' empathy — exactly right.

choices.en: That is a very difficult situation (formal).
choices.feedback: Stiff, textbook phrasing — no friend texts like this.

choices.en: I already finished all mine.
choices.feedback: Bragging while they're stressed — reads as rubbing it in.

turns.en: Right ㅠㅠ I'll probably have to pull an all-nighter

turns.prompt: Cheer them on and offer help.

choices.ko: 할 수 있어! 모르는 거 있음 물어봐
choices.en: You can do it! Ask me if you get stuck on anything
choices.feedback: Encouragement + an offer to help is warm and natural.

choices.en: Staying up all night is bad for your health (formal).
choices.feedback: Lecturing and formal — kills the supportive vibe.

choices.en: So how many assignments was it again?
choices.feedback: Just repeats a question they already answered.

turns.en: Thanks ㅠㅠ That really cheered me up.

turns.prompt: Tell them to hang in there.

choices.en: You got this!! Hit me up when you're done
choices.feedback: 화이팅 + 끝나면 연락해 is the classic casual send-off.

choices.en: Then I hope you work hard (formal).
choices.feedback: Overly formal — friends say 화이팅 or 파이팅.

choices.en: What's the assignment topic?
choices.feedback: Opens a new question when the chat is wrapping up.

title: Let's study together
situation: A friend texts that the exam is close and they have not started studying, so you suggest studying together.
tip: Proposing plans casually (~할래?, ~하자, 콜) and locking in details (몇 시? 어디서?) is how friends turn an idea into an actual hangout.

turns.ko: 아 시험 코앞인데 하나도 안 했어
turns.en: Ugh the exam's right around the corner and I haven't done a thing

turns.prompt: Say you're the same and suggest studying together.

choices.en: Same lol wanna study together?
choices.feedback: 나도 (relate) + 같이 공부할래? (proposal) is a perfect casual invite.

choices.en: How would it be to study together? (very formal).
choices.feedback: Textbook-formal — no friend phrases an invite like this.

choices.en: It's better to study alone.
choices.feedback: Shoots down the chance to make a plan together.

turns.en: Oh nice! Where should we do it?

turns.prompt: Suggest a cafe and ask if it works.

choices.ko: 학교 앞 카페 어때? 거기 조용하잖아
choices.en: How about the cafe by school? It's quiet there
choices.feedback: A concrete spot + 거기 조용하잖아 gives a reason and keeps it moving.

choices.en: You decide the place (formal).
choices.feedback: 당신 and 정하세요 are stiff — friends just throw out an idea.

choices.en: The library has no seats.
choices.feedback: Only says where NOT to go without suggesting anything.

turns.en: Deal! What time should we meet?

turns.prompt: Propose 2 PM and check it's okay.

choices.ko: 두 시 어때? 점심 먹고 가자
choices.en: How about 2? Let's go after lunch
choices.feedback: Names a time + 점심 먹고 가자 — natural and locks in the plan.

choices.en: I will see you at 2 PM (formal).
choices.feedback: 뵙겠습니다 is honorific — way too formal for a friend.

choices.en: I don't eat breakfast.
choices.feedback: Off-topic — they asked about the meeting time.

turns.prompt: Confirm and tell them to bring their notes.

choices.en: K, make sure you bring your notes lol
choices.feedback: ㅇㅋ + a quick casual reminder is exactly how friends sign off.

choices.en: Please bring your notes (formal).
choices.feedback: 지참해 주시기 바랍니다 sounds like an official notice — far too formal.

choices.en: By the way, what's the exam range?
choices.feedback: Opens a brand-new question just as you're saying bye.
